Added delinkDeadReferences() to strip (to plain text) any link whose target is denylisted or a directory-style reference. Gave each nested file distinct title frontmatter to avoid a nav-label collision with the skill's own index page. outputDir is now wiped (rmSync) at the start of every sync since content/skills/** is fully generated output, so a layout change doesn't leave stale pages from the previous shape alongside the new ones.

bugs.error_message: SessionStart hook emitted invalid JSON (JSONDecodeError: Expecting ',' delimiter) on every session, pre-dating this session's other changes
bugs.root_cause: superpowers_context is the only context block built in session-start.sh that skips escape_for_json() before being interpolated into the final printf JSON template — being fully static, it was presumably assumed quote-free, but it embeds a literal code example, { "skill": "<name>" }, whose two double-quote pairs were never escaped for the outer JSON envelope. Confirmed pre-existing by running the pre-merge commit (8a3b702): identical parse error at the identical byte offset, unrelated to the understand-anything staleness feature being added in this session.
bugs.fix: Escaped just the two offending quote pairs in place (source \" -> \\\", producing runtime \" instead of a bare ") rather than restructuring the whole string's bash quoting style — minimal, surgical change on a hook every session depends on. Added hooks/session-start.test.js (real subprocess invocation, asserts JSON.parse succeeds) as a regression test; more detail than bug-135's auto-detected entry for the same file.

bugs.error_message: N/A — silent data-loss bug caught by review, not a runtime error message
bugs.root_cause: Bash heredoc terminator (`EOF` under `<<'EOF'`) must be flush-left with zero leading whitespace to be recognized as a closer. The terminator was indented to match the surrounding markdown list-item nesting, so bash treated it as heredoc content instead of a closer, silently swallowing the rest of the script block (including the second heredoc and its own commands) into the first generated file.
bugs.fix: Dedented the heredoc body and terminator lines to column 0 while leaving surrounding command lines (the `cat > ... <<'EOF'` openers and the trailing `echo` line) at their normal indent — the correct, idiomatic convention for heredocs even inside indented code. Verified by actually extracting and executing the block (both pre-fix and post-fix), not just visual inspection.

bugs.error_message: N/A — security/data-integrity finding from code review, not a runtime error
bugs.root_cause: appendObservation/resolveObservation interpolated free-form field text directly into a markdown log with no validation. A field value containing a line matching the log's own header pattern (`### Observation N:`) would inject a forged header, corrupting the numbering invariant every other function relies on. Additionally, the header-count integrity check in resolveObservation/archiveObservations ran AFTER the corrupting writeFileSync, so it only detected damage rather than preventing it.
bugs.fix: Added assertNoHeaderInjection() to reject (throw before any lock/write) any field containing a header-pattern line; moved the header-count invariant check to run against in-memory content BEFORE writeFileSync in all three mutating functions (append/resolve/archive), so a bad result never reaches disk.

bugs.error_message: N/A — logic bug found in whole-branch review, not a runtime error
bugs.root_cause: When inserting a new Phase 3 section between an existing conditional Phase 2 and the final Report step, Phase 2's skip-condition target was updated to the new Report step's arithmetic position — but that bypassed Phase 3 entirely in the common case (Phase 2 not firing), since Phase 3 sits between Phase 2 and Report. The skip needed to land on Phase 3's own independent due-for-review gate, not jump past it to Report.
bugs.fix: Changed the skip target from the Report step to Phase 3's first step (which has its own independent 'is a review due?' check), so Phase 2 skipping doesn't also skip Phase 3.

bugs.error_message: cerebrum-write-guard.js false-positived 'another session wrote to cerebrum.md' on the session's own routine second edit
bugs.root_cause: A PreToolUse hook recorded cerebrum.md's mtime as its baseline BEFORE the gated Edit/Write actually landed. Since the tool lands its write immediately after, the file's real mtime bumps, and the hook's own next invocation compared that bumped mtime against its own stale pre-edit baseline, false-positiving on its own prior edit rather than a genuine cross-session write.
bugs.fix: Split marker-writing into a new PostToolUse companion hook (cerebrum-write-guard-post.js) that records the mtime AFTER the write lands; the PreToolUse hook became read-only (compare only, never write). A prior 'regression test' for this didn't actually discriminate old vs new behavior (a runPost() call in the test masked the difference either way) — fixed with a direct assertion that the PreToolUse hook itself never creates the marker file.

bugs.error_message: A submodule-file edit task's commit landed in the PRIMARY checkout's superpowers submodule instead of an isolated worktree copy
bugs.root_cause: Fresh git worktrees (via native EnterWorktree or `git worktree add`) do not auto-initialize submodules. A subagent dispatched to edit a submodule-symlinked skill file found the worktree's own superpowers/ directory empty and, rather than initializing it, ended up committing directly into /Users/paulmckay/.claude/superpowers (the main checkout) on branch main — exactly the worktree-isolation failure this project's own plan existed to prevent, recurring during its own implementation.
bugs.fix: Initialized the submodule inside the worktree (git submodule update --init superpowers), fetched the correct local-only base commit from the main checkout (git submodule update --init alone can't resolve a commit that only exists in local-customizations history, not upstream), then used scripts/submodule-transfer.sh to bring the stray commit in as an isolated copy on local-customizations. Left the main checkout's own commit in place (non-destructive, user-approved) and advanced its local-customizations pointer to match. A second submodule task later in the same session correctly initialized the submodule upfront and had no incident.

bugs.error_message: plugin-health-check-gate.sh: a corrupted (non-numeric) gate-file timestamp crashed the script permanently with no self-heal, and its own test suite couldn't have caught a broken skip condition
bugs.root_cause: Under `set -euo pipefail`, `ELAPSED=$(( NOW - LAST ))` on a non-numeric LAST value crashed the script BEFORE it reached the line that rewrites the gate file — so every future run hit the identical crash with no path to recovery. Separately, the test asserting the 24h skip logic only checked the wrapped command's exit code, which the script's own `|| true` neutralizes regardless of whether the skip logic actually fired — proven by disabling the skip branch entirely and watching the test still pass.
bugs.fix: Added a `[[ "$LAST" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]` guard before the arithmetic — a non-numeric value now falls through to the normal write+run path, which overwrites the bad value (self-heal). Rewrote the test to have the stubbed script write a sentinel file instead of relying on exit code, so non-invocation is actually proven; verified by re-running the new test against a deliberately-broken skip condition and confirming it now fails.

bugs.error_message: New skill's agents/openai.yaml (and skills/ba-agent/agents/ba.md) never appeared as untracked in git status; silently absent from a fresh clone
bugs.root_cause: The `Agents/` line in .gitignore (meant only for the root-level ~/.claude/Agents/<agent-name>/ custom-agent workspace directory) had no leading slash, so gitignore treated it as unanchored and matched at any depth. Combined with this repo's case-insensitive filesystem (macOS APFS default) and git's core.ignorecase, it also silently matched-and-ignored any nested lowercase agents/ directory belonging to an installed skill (skills/make-interfaces-feel-better/agents/, skills/ba-agent/agents/). Files inside such directories were untracked but invisible to plain `git status` (only visible via `git status --ignored` or `git check-ignore -v <path>`), so they could sit unrecovered indefinitely.
bugs.fix: Anchored the pattern to `/Agents/` in .gitignore so it only matches the intended root-level directory. Recovered the one live casualty found (`skills/ba-agent/agents/ba.md`) with `git add -f`. Audited the rest of the repo with `git status --ignored --short | grep '^!!'` for other orphans under nested agents/ paths -- none found.

Most likely cause: the harness session_id rotated across the conversation span (spanning 2026-08-09 through 2026-08-11, implying compaction/resumption events), so the marker written under an earlier session_id is invisible to a gate check running under a later one.
bugs.fix: Re-invoked the grilling skill under the current session_id to write a fresh marker (confirmed via direct file check afterward), then proceeded to writing-plans. No code fix applied — the underlying gap (no cross-session-id carryover, no marker TTL/cleanup visibility) is a known limitation of the session-scoped marker design, not something patched here.

bugs.error_message: ENOBUFS crash running wolf-debt-scan.js inside a live Claude Code session
bugs.root_cause: grepMarkers() excludes .wolf, .superpowers, and file-history as Claude Code self-referential runtime state, but omitted projects/ (session transcripts + persisted tool-output caches). Only *.jsonl was excluded by extension, so non-jsonl files under projects/ (e.g. tool-results/*.txt) matched. Running the scanner mid-session caches its own grep output into one of these files, which then matches the next scan, snowballing past execFileSync default maxBuffer and crashing with ENOBUFS.
bugs.fix: Added '--exclude-dir=projects' to the grep args alongside the existing .wolf/.superpowers/file-history exclusions. Added regression test covering a non-jsonl file under projects/.

bugs.error_message: Free-text values interpolated into String.replace()'s replacement-string argument get pattern-expanded
bugs.root_cause: resolveObservation() built its Status-line and Evidence-line replacements as template strings passed directly as the second argument to String.prototype.replace(). JS treats $1, $&, $`, $' as special replacement patterns in that position, so any note/evidence text containing a literal $ followed by a digit or one of those characters silently mangled the written line instead of being written verbatim.
bugs.fix: Switched both .replace() calls to use a function replacer instead of a template string — a function's return value is used verbatim, with no pattern expansion. Caught by a whole-branch code review, not the original implementer or task-scoped reviewer; regression test added asserting a literal $1/$& string survives unmangled.

bugs.error_message: PostToolUseFailure hook never fires: wrong payload field and output channel
bugs.root_cause: Assumed the stdin payload field was `tool_error` and that stdout+exit(0) with hookSpecificOutput reached the model, matching the pattern used by other hook events in this repo (and matching what a claude-code-guide subagent claimed when asked). The real PostToolUseFailure contract uses field `error` (not `tool_error`) and requires stderr+exit(2) for the model to see the message, per the CLI's own embedded docs.
bugs.fix: Verified the real contract by running `strings` on the installed CLI binary (~/.local/share/claude/versions/<ver>) and grepping for the event name / 'Input to command is JSON with...' text. Changed input.tool_error -> input.error, and switched output from stdout+exit(0) JSON to process.stderr.write(...) + process.exit(2).

bugs.error_message: Re-read gate never blocks anything: settings.json passes a nonexistent env var
bugs.root_cause: settings.json's PreToolUse/Read entry invoked the hook with "${TOOL_INPUT_PATH:-}" "${CLAUDE_CWD:-.}" as argv. TOOL_INPUT_PATH does not exist anywhere in the Claude Code CLI (confirmed via `strings` on the installed binary: zero occurrences, no TOOL_INPUT_-prefixed variable family at all) -- it always expanded to an empty string via bash's :- fallback, so the hook exited immediately on every invocation. Predated the current session's hook-hardening work entirely; existed since the hook was first wired.
bugs.fix: Rewired hooks/pre-read-check.js to read tool_input.file_path and cwd from stdin JSON (readStdin() from scripts/hook-input.js), matching every other hook in the repo, and removed the broken argv substitution from settings.json's command string. Verified empirically live: read the same unchanged file twice in a row post-fix -> second read correctly blocked.

bugs.error_message: Verification script's grep -q "\$$s" reports every case as MISSING even when the content is present
bugs.root_cause: Inside bash double quotes, \$ collapses to a literal $ before grep ever receives the argument, so the pattern passed to grep is bare $name instead of an escaped-dollar-then-name literal. Mid-pattern behavior for a bare $ is inconsistent across grep implementations, and here it produced a silent false negative rather than an error, on every single case tested.
bugs.fix: Use single-quote + concatenation to preserve the backslash: grep -q '\$'"$s" file. Verified by re-running the corrected loop for all 16 required names and getting genuinely empty (passing) output, confirmed independently against a direct grep and against a code-reviewer subagent's diff read.
